## Introduction

## Reading in the Data

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)

# read in data
# use 'Latin1' for locale 
bike_data <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale = locale(encoding = "Latin1"))
```

## Checking the Data (EDA)

```{r}
# check for any missing values (#1)
colSums(is.na(bike_data))

# check structure (#2) ; (can also use 'glimpse' which has a nicer output)
str(bike_data)
glimpse(bike_data)

# convert 'Date' column from chr into actual dates (day/month/year) & confirm change (#3) 
bike_data$Date <- dmy(trimws(bike_data$Date))
glimpse(bike_data)

# take a look at data itself
head(bike_data)

# do summary stats for numeric columns (#2)
summary(bike_data)

# check unique values for categorical variables (#2)
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# turn character variables into factors (Seasons, Holiday, Functioning Day) and check levels (#4)

bike_data$Seasons <- factor(bike_data$Seasons)
levels(bike_data$Seasons)

bike_data$Holiday <- factor(bike_data$Holiday)
levels(bike_data$Holiday)

bike_data$`Functioning Day` <- factor(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
levels(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# double check to make sure structure looks good, specifically for date and factors w/ levels 
str(bike_data)

# rename all variables for easier use & confirm change (#5)
names(bike_data)

bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    date = Date,
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
    seasons = Seasons,
    holiday = Holiday,
    functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
  )

names(bike_data)

# create summary statistics for numeric variables (#6)
bike_data |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# create summary statistics for categorical variables using bike rental count (#6)  

# by season
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by functioning day
bike_data |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# exclude non-functioning observations since rentals won't happen on those days (#6)
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes")

# summarize across hours so each day has one observation (#7)
daily_bike <- bike_data |>
  # group by date, seasons, and holiday
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  
  # find sum of bike_count, rainfall, & snowfall
  summarise(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    
    # find mean of other weather-related variables
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    
    .groups = "drop" # removes grouping
  )

# check new dataset 
glimpse(daily_bike)

# recreate basic summary stats (#8) 

# numeric variables
daily_bike |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# categorical variables   

# by season
daily_bike |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
daily_bike |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# create plots to explore relationships (#8)

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across seasons
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = seasons, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) + 
  theme_grey()

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across holidays and non-holidays
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = holiday, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Holiday",
    x = "Holiday (Y/N)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# scatterplot: compare daily bike rentals across temperature 
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = temp, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm"
    ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bike Rentals vs. Temperature",
    x = "Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# report correlation between numeric variables (#8)
daily_bike |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs") |>
  round(2) |>
  as.data.frame() |> # nicer to look at than a matrix, to me personally  
  rownames_to_column(var = "Variable")
```

## Splitting the Data
```{r}
# set seed for reproduction
set.seed(13)

# split data into training and test set (75/25 split) & use 'strata' to stratify the split on 'seasons'
split_bike <- initial_split(
  daily_bike,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

train_bike <- training(split_bike)
test_bike <- testing(split_bike)

# check number of observations for 75/25 split
nrow(train_bike$seasons)
nrow(test_bike$seasons)
```
